fixes.explanation: The verse doesn't say that. Paul writes, "We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one." Nothing at all is a pretty strong way to put it. It's a lot of fuss over something the verse calls nothing at all.

Right, the verse says, "We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world…" It adds that there is no God but one (1 Corinthians 8:4). So False is the pick, however fancy the idol looks. A statue can have the best paint job in town and still be nothing at all in the world.

problems.problem: Saying Paul says the opposite attributes the claim that an idol is not a real power to him, beyond what 1 Corinthians 8:4 states.
Saying the statement is false attributes the claim that an idol is not a real power to Paul, beyond what 1 Corinthians 8:4 states.
